title: The Ladder Is Missing Rungs: Engineering Progression When AI Ate the Middle
gist: Alasdair Allan argues AI coding tools erode the junior-to-senior pipeline: METR, Anthropic and labor data show skill formation stunted, work shifting to supervision and entry-level hiring slowing, creating a 'supervision paradox' with no ready fix.

insights.claim: Dario Amodei's claim that AI writes 90% of code overstated reality; Redwood Research found about 50% of committed code, while Google reports just over 25% and Microsoft about 30%.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Vendor adoption claims are inflated; discount headline percentages.
insights.locator: A detailed analysis by Redwood Research

insights.claim: Anthropic engineers use Claude for 59% of daily work, self-report 50% productivity gains, and roughly 4% of GitHub commits are authored by Claude Code.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Real but self-reported usage; indicates the scale of Claude Code share.

insights.claim: METR's RCT found experienced developers took 19% longer with AI while predicting 24% faster and afterwards believing 20% faster, a 43-point perception gap.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Self-reported productivity is unreliable; demand measured outcomes.

insights.claim: METR's follow-up could not run because developers refused to work without AI, so the tool went from optional to load-bearing before its effects were understood.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Dependency means measuring AI productivity is now hard.
insights.quote: You can't do a controlled trial if there's no control.
insights.locator: In February this year, METR tried

insights.claim: Most recent coding-tool gains come from tighter feedback loops and architecture around models, not intelligence.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Scaffolding and tooling companies capture value alongside model providers.
insights.locator: To be clear, the last four to five months

insights.claim: METR's 50% time horizon doubled roughly every seven months since 2019 and about every four months since 2024; AI succeeds near 100% below four minutes, about 50% at one hour and below 10% beyond four hours.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Capability trend gives a base for forecasting task automation; extrapolation to a full workday by 2027 is flagged as speculative.

insights.claim: About 50% of AI pull requests that passed tests would not be merged by maintainers, and maintainers needed about 42 minutes to fix an AI PR, roughly a third of human time.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Benchmarks overstate real-world capability; review overhead is hidden cost.
insights.quote: AI can implement core functionality, but consistently fails with craft

insights.claim: Faros AI telemetry on about 10,000 developers found high AI adoption teams complete 21% more tasks and merge 98% more PRs, but PR review time rises 91%, bugs per developer 9% and PR size 154%.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Bottleneck shifts to code review; watch review and QA tooling.

insights.claim: GitClear's analysis of 211 million lines found AI adoption raised code volume 10% while refactoring fell 60%, copy-paste rose 48% and churn rose 44%.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Quality metrics are deteriorating, implying future maintenance debt.

themes.theme: Skill formation and the supervision paradox

insights.claim: In Anthropic's RCT of 52 mostly junior engineers learning Trio, AI users were not significantly faster (p=0.391) but scored 17% lower on the mastery quiz (50% vs 67%, p=0.01), with the largest gap on debugging.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: AI assistance may trade learning for nothing, undermining future verification skills.
insights.locator: Contrast this to a randomized control trial

insights.claim: Full delegation, progressive reliance and AI-debugging-AI patterns all scored below 40% versus 67% for the unassisted group.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Usage pattern, not tool use alone, determines learning loss.

insights.claim: The supervision paradox holds that using AI requires supervision, and supervision requires coding skills that atrophy from AI overuse.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Long-term quality of AI-assisted software depends on preserving human expertise.
insights.quote: using AI requires supervision, and supervision requires the very coding skills that atrophy from AI overuse
insights.locator: Anthropic points out this as a paradox

insights.claim: AI tends to help already-skilled developers while giving novices output without understanding; DX's 20,000-developer data show senior engineers save the most time despite low adoption.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Productivity benefit accrues to experienced engineers.

insights.claim: Anthropic engineers ask 80-90% of questions to Claude rather than colleagues, losing incidental mentoring from debugging sessions with senior peers.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Erodes tacit knowledge transfer inside teams.

insights.claim: In December 2025 Amazon's Kiro agent, with operator-level permissions, reportedly chose to delete and recreate AWS Cost Explorer's environment, causing a 13-hour recovery in one China region, which Amazon called user error.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Agents with permissions but no production judgment are operational risk.
insights.quote: AI had the permissions. It lacked the battle scars.

insights.claim: Amazon disputes reports of AI-driven retail outages and says only one incident involved AI, via an engineer following inaccurate advice an AI inferred from an outdated wiki, and denies new approval requirements.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Narrative disputed; the confirmed case is still a context-curation failure.

insights.claim: Stale documentation treated with equal weight in the context window is a context failure, so codified context must be treated as infrastructure; one project's context reached 26,000 lines, more than the code.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Context curation is the new engineering discipline and a tooling opportunity.
insights.locator: This is the distinction between prompt engineering

insights.claim: For brownfield systems the honest sequence is observe production, extract behavioral contracts, encode system tests, then bring in the agent, using characterization tests, contract testing, traffic shadowing and canary analysis.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Legacy modernization with AI needs test-first contracts.
insights.locator: The honest sequence for non-greenfield systems

insights.claim: Anthropic's labor study shows computer programmers at 74.5% observed exposure and computer and math occupations at 94% theoretical but only 33% observed coverage.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Large unrealized gap implies further displacement potential.
insights.locator: Computer programmers are the most exposed

insights.claim: Unemployment in AI-exposed occupations has not diverged since ChatGPT, but job finding for 22-25-year-olds in exposed roles fell about 14% and ADP data show 6-16% employment declines, driven by slowed hiring.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Entry-level hiring, not layoffs, is the channel; weak statistical significance.
insights.locator: The hiring of young workers has slowed

insights.claim: BLS growth projections drop 0.6 percentage points per 10-point rise in AI task coverage.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Official projections already price in displacement for exposed occupations.

insights.claim: Amazon laid off 14,000 corporate workers in October and 16,000 more in January.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Large-cap workforce cuts coincide with AI adoption narrative.

insights.claim: Proposed remedies include structured learning paths and rotation through fundamentals like medical residencies, requiring understanding before AI help, measuring understanding not velocity, and treating context as infrastructure.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Companies that invest in training may keep senior capacity; most won't.
insights.locator: There are some things we can do now

insights.claim: Only 27% of Claude-assisted work is from tasks that would not otherwise have been done, offering one escape: expanded demand for software rather than fewer developers.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Jevons-style demand growth could offset headcount.
insights.locator: Anthropic's data offers one possible escape

insights.claim: The real question is not whether to adopt AI but how to train engineers who can supervise what they never learned to do.
insights.speaker: Alasdair Allan
insights.so_what: Talent pipeline risk is a long-run constraint on AI coding value.
insights.locator: The question is not whether to adopt AI
